narrative:

Your total years of experience stands out as the strongest factor pushing the model toward expecting you to leave. With over 11 years across your career, you have significantly more experience than most employees the model predicts will stay—only 14.7% of stayers have this level of seniority. The model sees this as a sign that you have the background to pursue better opportunities elsewhere.

Next, the fact that you have not received other job offers while at this company actually works in your favor, pulling the prediction slightly back toward staying. Most employees the model expects to remain also report no external offers, so this aligns you with the “stayer” group on this point.

Your relatively short time in your current role (1-5 years) is the third most influential factor and pushes the prediction back toward leaving. This tenure is actually typical among both groups, but combined with your high overall experience, the model interprets it as a sign you may still be evaluating whether this organization is the right long-term fit.

The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you openly and exploring whether additional recognition, better work-life support, or clearer promotion paths could increase your commitment. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying feel more rewarding.
